ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01 by intercepting every git call from `gt sync --no-interactive` (gt 1.8.6); fact 3 CORRECTED and fact 5 ADDED 2026-08-02 after two independent re-measurements (27 runs + a 9,289-log corpus sweep). An earlier version of this note stated fact 3 wrongly.

```
GIT: fetch --no-write-fetch-head --progress --no-tags -f origin refs/heads/main:refs/gt-fetch-head/main
GIT: rev-parse refs/gt-fetch-head/main
GIT: update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main b6f3974...
GIT: merge-base --is-ancestor main b6f3974...
GIT: -C /…/gt-main-co reset -q --keep b6f3974... --
```

1. gt WRITES `refs/remotes/<remote>/<trunk>` itself from its own fetch, before it attempts to move the local branch — so the remote-tracking ref is the oracle gt itself treats as ground truth. This is why ccx vcs restack compares against it rather than the local ref.

2. gt does NOT hit gits "cannot force update the branch used by worktree" refusal, because it does not use `git branch -f`. It runs `git -C <sibling-worktree> reset -q --keep` — it hard-resets ANOTHER working copys tree without asking. On a clean sibling this SUCCEEDS and local trunk advances.

3. CORRECTED — the original claim ("gt prints ERROR: Cannot pull trunk due to conflicting unstaged changes. and STILL EXITS 0") is FALSE. Two DISTINCT messages were conflated:
   - `ERROR: Cannot pull trunk due to conflicting unstaged changes. ` (stderr, trailing space): remote trunk IS fast-forwardable but the worktree holding trunk is dirty, so gts `reset --keep` fails. **Exit 1, universally** — 19 configurations incl. --no-interactive, --interactive, -q, --force, --no-restack, -d, -a, and a real PTY.
   - `WARNING: main could not be fast-forwarded.` (stderr): local trunk has DIVERGED from remote — a different path that never reaches the holder reset. **Exit 0 only when the overwrite proceeds** (`--force`, or an interactive TTY answering yes); under `--no-interactive` it is exit 1.

4. `Did not restack branch <b> because it is checked out in worktree <w>.` is printed to **stdout** at **exit 0**, stderr empty. gtSyncSkipped parses this correctly.

5. THE REAL exit-0-on-STDERR CASE, and the one that justifies surfacing stderr diagnostics at exit 0:
   `WARNING: <branch> could not be restacked cleanly.` on **stderr**, **EXIT 0**, with stdouts restack section EMPTY. Fires under plain `gt sync --no-interactive` (non-TTY pipes, no --force) when a stack branch and trunk edit the same line and trunk advances: sync fast-forwards trunk, cannot restack the branch, warns, exits 0. Confirmed in a lab AND by 7 occurrences across 9,289 real gt debug logs — a live production case. gt also prints an actionable remediation line (`Please resolve conflicts...`) alongside it, which is worth surfacing together with the warning rather than alone.

So: gt carries meaning at exit 0 on BOTH streams — decline lines on stdout (fact 4), restack-cleanly warnings on stderr (fact 5). A wrapper reading only the exit code, or only one stream, misses real failures.

METHOD WARNINGS:
- `strings` on the gt binary is useless — it is a packed 86 MB Mach-O, and known-emitted strings ("Trunk set to", "Authenticated as") return zero matches. Any static-grep evidence about gts messages is void; measure by running it.
- Reaching the trunk-pull stage offline requires adding "owner"/"name" to .git/.graphite_repo_config (undocumented but accepted). git `insteadOf` rewriting does NOT work — gt reads the rewritten URL.
- gt 1.8.6 is the LATEST published version, so the `WARNING: Your Graphite CLI is out of date.` nag cannot currently fire; any fixture using it models an untriggerable message.
